mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals supply-side disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drop does not correlate with subsequent supply-side issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% YoY, the combination signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% YoY and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) also increase, it signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% YoY and RSAFS increases
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of HOUST and RSAFS increases does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, especially in a regime of low inflation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with subsequent market performance in low inflation regimes.
